archive.title: Trump ordered to answer questions under oath in BBC lawsuit
archive.summary: A US judge has ordered President Donald Trump to answer questions under oath in his defamation lawsuit against the BBC by 11 December. Trump is suing the BBC over an episode of Panorama that edited together two different sections of a speech he gave before the riot at the US Capitol in 2021. Trump cancelled a previous deposition - or interview under oath - on 16 October, citing "matters of national importance". But a lawyer representing the BBC said in court that Trump was campaigning in Georgia that day and had "prioritised that" over answering the questions.

Trump is suing the BBC over an episode of Panorama that edited together two different sections of a speech he gave before the riot at the US Capitol in 2021. Trump cancelled a previous deposition - or interview under oath - on 16 October, citing "matters of national importance". But a lawyer representing the BBC said in court that Trump was campaigning in Georgia that day and had "prioritised that" over answering the questions. President Trump's lawsuit against the BBC is in the phase known as "discovery", where the two sides provide internal or other records that could form evidence. Charles Tobin, a lawyer for the BBC, told a court in Miami on Thursday that with two months left in the discovery period, Trump had still not completed a deposition. The judge in the case, US Magistrate Judge Enjoliqué Lett, said that Trump must sit for the deposition by 11 December, unless the discovery period is extended.

archive.title: Websites taken down as critical PHP cyber-security update issued
archive.summary: The Finnish government, Edinburgh council and the BBC are among those to have taken down sites and pages ahead of a software update to a programming language which underpins many online services. Two critical vulnerabilities have been found with the PHP programming language, which is widely used across the internet. A fix was issued on Wednesday afternoon. The flaws were discovered by AI, with cyber-security firm Wiz saying they were the "most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered" by the tech, which is reshaping the cyber landscape. Multiple national cyber-security agencies have urged organisations to rapidly adopt the updates, or consider taking their websites offline.

archive.summary: Heartbleed is the name of a critical vulnerability in the OpenSSL cryptography library. In 2014, it came under mass exploitation. Exploits let many unaffiliated hackers decrypt TLS-protected exchanges between parties. They also recovered private TLS certificate keys, session cookies, and passwords. The attacks compromised thousands of servers, some belonging to large companies and government agencies around the world. Recovery required a long series of steps that took years. archive.title: UNC-Chapel Hill strikes bargain with Trump administration to end probes
archive.summary: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill on Monday struck a deal with the Trump administration to end federal investigations into its handling of alleged campus antisemitism and civil rights violations. Under the terms, the highly selective public flagship will share with the federal government years’ worth data on civil rights complaints and adopt new policies, ranging from admissions changes to student activity oversight. In exchange, the U.S. departments of Justice and Education will end more than a dozen active civil rights probes into the university. UNC-Chapel Hill did not admit wrongdoing under the agreement, and the federal government said it does not intend to dictate the "content of academic speech or curricula" at the university.
archive.editorialText: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill on Monday struck a deal with the Trump administration to end federal investigations into its handling of alleged campus antisemitism and civil rights violations. Under the terms, the highly selective public flagship will share with the federal government years’ worth data on civil rights complaints and adopt new policies, ranging from admissions changes to student activity oversight. In exchange, the U.S. departments of Justice and Education will end more than a dozen active civil rights probes into the university. UNC-Chapel Hill did not admit wrongdoing under the agreement, and the federal government said it does not intend to dictate the "content of academic speech or curricula" at the university. Unlike most of the deals the Trump administration has struck, UNC-Chapel Hill will not pay a monetary settlement. UNC-Chapel Hill faced 18 active Title VI investigations from the Education Department dating back to 2019, "spanning the Biden and Trump administrations," according to the university. Title VI bars institutions that receive federal funding from discriminating on the basis of race, color or national origin.
